diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is operating close to its shared capacity during busy periods, with current traffic at 912 Mbps and peak traffic at 948 Mbps versus a roughly 1 Gbps PON limit. This explains the evening-only throughput degradation.
evidence: The subscriber is currently online and responding, with normal RX power of -21.27 dBm and TX power of 2.37 dBm.

Seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable; RX remains in the normal band, TX remains within the calibrated normal range, and TX bias current is stable. There is no evidence of fibre or laser degradation.
Distance is constant at 167, so there is no fibre-path change.
All probed peers on EPON0/7 are online and responding, so the issue is not an ONU dropout, splitter failure, or whole-port outage.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and OID queries, while its CPU, memory, and temperature are not indicative of an OLT failure.
The subscriber has only 2 sessions in 24 hours, with an average duration of 711 minutes, so this is not session flapping or an authentication fault.
RADIUS, line ID, IP assignment, and VLAN 1017 are consistent and correctly provisioned.
EPON0/7 is carrying 912 Mbps currently, with a 948 Mbps peak and a 488 Mbps average. Near-gigabit peaks on a shared EPON port match the customer's evening-only slowdown and indicate PON congestion.

remediation.action: Review per-ONU utilization and confirm evening saturation, then reduce contention by migrating customers to another PON, splitting or upgrading the PON capacity, and applying appropriate bandwidth scheduling or QoS. Continue monitoring peak utilization and customer throughput after remediation.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
